title: Flatness off a μH[n−2+α]-null set for an abstract measure class with domains, via Appendix A.4 (parent steps 3–4)
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, Λ ∈ ℝ, let 𝓜 be a set of measures on ℝ^P and D a map from measures on ℝ^P to subsets of ℝ^P. For a measure μ on ℝ^P and x ∈ ℝ^P let dens μ x := (limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n)).toReal (limsup in [0, ∞] along ρ → 0⁺, ω_n = unitBallVolume n; in the Lean statement dens is a universally quantified function fixed by this defining equation); for y ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, μ^{y,λ} := ofReal(λ^{−n})•μ.map(η_{y,λ}) (= λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ, η_{y,λ} = dilation y λ); spt μ := {w : μ(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0}; μ_j → μ vaguely means ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Assume (M1) every μ ∈ 𝓜 is finite on compact sets; (M2) every μ ∈ 𝓜 equals Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ dens μ) (Hⁿ = μHE[n]); (M3) for μ ∈ 𝓜, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ: μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 and D(μ^{y,λ}) = η_{y,λ}(D μ); (M4) for μ ∈ 𝓜, |y| < 1 and every strictly decreasing sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0 there are a strictly increasing sub : ℕ → ℕ and ν ∈ 𝓜 with dens ν(tw) = dens ν(w) for all t > 0 and w, and μ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}} → ν vaguely; (M5) for μ ∈ 𝓜, D μ is open and contains B_2(0); (M6) if μ ∈ 𝓜, μ_j ∈ 𝓜 (j ∈ ℕ) and μ_j → μ vaguely, then every compact K ⊆ D μ satisfies K ⊆ D(μ_j) for all large j; (M7) for μ ∈ 𝓜, y ∈ spt μ and ρ > 0 with closedBall y ρ ⊆ D μ: e^{−Λρ}·ω_nρ^n ≤ μ(B_ρ(y)); (M8) if ν ∈ 𝓜 and L is a linear subspace with dim L + 1 = n and dens ν(y + tw) = dens ν(w) for all y ∈ L, t > 0 and w, then spt ν ⊆ Q for some n-dimensional linear subspace Q; (M9) if ν ∈ 𝓜 and dens ν(tw) = dens ν(w) for all t > 0 and w, then D ν = ℝ^P. Then for every μ ∈ 𝓜 and every β > 0 there is a set Z ⊆ ℝ^P such that Z = ∅ if n = 1, μH[n − 2 + α](Z) = 0 for every real α > 0, and every w ∈ B_1(0) ∩ spt μ with w ∉ Z is β-flat in D μ: there are ρ > 0 with B_ρ(w) ⊆ D μ, an n-dimensional linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P and s < βρ such that |(y − w) − p_Q(y − w)| ≤ s for every y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_ρ(w) (p_Q = Q.starProjection).
